newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan body to let govt delay BOJ decisions.
newsitem.headline: Japan body to let govt delay BOJ decisions.

text.p: A government committee discussing ways to reform the the Bank of Japan (BOJ) is considering allowing the government to keep its right to intervene in decisions made by the central bank, committee chairman Ryuichiro Tachi told reporters on Friday.
"We are considering allowing the right of the government to put on hold decisions (made by the BOJ's policy board)," Tachi said, although he said details will be decided later.
Currently, the government can put on hold decisions by the BOJ policy board if its views differ from that of the BOJ.
The BOJ is considered to have less independence than central banks in other major industrialised nations.
Tachi said the BOJ reforms should be carried out in a way which enables the government to voice its views to the BOJ policy board, including putting its decisions on hold.
A ministry official told reporters that putting a decision on hold did not mean the government was rejecting the BOJ decision, but was asking them to discuss the matter again.
The committee members also agreed that government representatives should be allowed to attend the meetings if deemed necessary, Tachi said.
They currently attend the meetings but do not vote.
They also agreed that the BOJ's inspection of financial firms should be given some kind of legal backing, he said.
